title: Daytime Flights from Asia to Australia
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Cathay Pacific offers daytime flights from Hong Kong to multiple Australian cities. Photo: Cathay Pacific.
If you often fly to or from Asia with Qantas, you’ve probably noticed that most of Qantas’ flights from Asia back to Australia operate overnight. In the other direction, most of Qantas’ outbound flights from Australia to Asia are day flights.
Almost all of Qantas’ flights from Asia to Australia operate overnight. Photo: Matt Graham.
Most of Jetstar and Virgin Australia’s flights from Asia to Australia (except for some of the flights from Bali) are also redeye flights.
Qantas’ Asian schedules are perfect for people who prefer overnight flights back to Australia. But if you prefer daytime flights, there are other options from Asia to Australia that could be more convenient if you’re prepared to fly with other airlines. There are also a small number of daytime options on Qantas, e.g. from Tokyo to Australia.
This article lists all of the daytime flights currently available from Asia to Australia, sorted by Australian airport. For each route listed below, we’ve included the airline, flight number and schedule. Note that the schedules are subject to change, and may vary slightly on different days of the week or during daylight savings.

Daytime flights from Asia to Brisbane
Daytime flights from Asia to Cairns
Daytime flights from Asia to Darwin
Daytime flights from Asia to Melbourne
Note that Korean Air’s Seoul-Melbourne route and Qantas’ new daytime Tokyo-Melbourne flight are both seasonal, running during the Australian summer.
Daytime flights from Asia to Perth
Currently, most of the flights operating from Denpasar (Bali) to Perth are daytime flights. Jetstar, Batik Air, TransNusa and Indonesia AirAsia all have regular flights on this route, so we won’t list all of these flights here.
